subject: Exec approval request: retroactive rate-lock + limited uplift for NovoMed
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval request: retroactive rate-lock + limited uplift for NovoMed

Team —

Short version: NovoMed (prospect -> committed customer) is asking for a retroactive 3-year rate lock that would backdate to Jan 1, 2026 in exchange for a firm ARR commitment of $2.4M/year (volume tiers aligned to our standard). They want an uplift cap no greater than 5% per year and a renewal protection clause (no forced market-rate step-up at renewal for the length of the contract). Procurement is finalizing signature next week and has made this a gating term.

Why this matters: the deal moves a strategic healthcare account with a strong PLG adoption signal across three business units (billing, intake, analytics). Losing momentum will almost certainly push us to Q4 or later. The requested concessions are outside our standard uplift policy (we typically allow a 2% annual adjustment and do not backdate rate locks).

Numbers:
- Proposed term: 3 years, Jan 1, 2026 — Dec 31, 2028
- Committed ARR: $2.4M/year (annual billing)
- Proposed initial discount vs list: 18% first-year effective
- Requested uplift cap: 5%/year (cumulative cap: ~10.25% over two increases)
- Requested renewal protection: no >market uplift on first renewal after term end (customer wants an explicit clause)

Risks / ask:
- This sets a precedent for future health-system negotiations if we agree to retroactive rate locks.
- Legal needs to sign off on renewal language to avoid perpetual grandfathering.

Attachments: proposal & SOW redline are attached.

Requesting: senior exec approval (sales leadership / finance signoff) to accept the retroactive rate-lock + 5% uplift cap with the following mandatory mitigations:
1) Add an annual true-up clause tied to usage bands (we keep overage protection).
2) Limit renewal protection to a single renewal term and include a termination for material SLA breach.
3) Add a 12-month escrow/holdback for first-year credits (optional if legal insists).

Can you weigh in? I'm recommending conditional approval if Legal inserts the termination/true-up language and Finance confirms the unit economics (margins at 18% discount with our expected token mix). If approved, I'll push DocuSign and route procurement.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Exec approval request: retroactive rate-lock + limited uplift for NovoMed

Diego —

Thanks for the writeup and the attached redline. A few quick thoughts from Deal Desk perspective:

- Finance flag: 18% effective discount on a $2.4M ARR commitment reduces our projected gross margin below the acceptable corridor if they skew heavily to embeddings (high-cost tokens). Jordan, can you pull the projected token mix and margin by band?
- Legal flag: retroactive rate-lock language has to be tightly scoped (no backdoor perpetual grandfathering). We should scope renewal protection to "first renewal" only and add an explicit market-adjustment floor (e.g., we can apply an inflation index + cap, not open-ended).
- Operational guardrail: require a quarterly usage report and an overage tranche pricing to prevent unexpected load.

Mitigations suggested (attached): SOW redline with a 5% uplift cap, a one-time renewal protection for the immediate renewal only, and a 12-month credit escrow tied to uptime/SLA targets. See SOW_NovoMed_redline.docx.

If Finance confirms margins and Legal gives the redline thumbs-up, I recommend we route for Laura's exec signoff with the three standard guardrails in place.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Diego —

I ran a quick economics scan with Finance ops: the deal is doable if we lock the following constraints into the contract:

1) Uplift cap at 5%/year (explicit) — accepted.
2) Renewal protection limited to the first renewal only (not perpetual) — accepted.
3) Annual usage true-up & overage buckets retained — mandatory.
4) Add a bilateral termination right for material SLA or data security breach during the term — mandatory.

With these constraints and a 12-month credit escrow for the first year, the modeled gross margin stays within an acceptable range (assuming the token mix matches the one Diego provided).

I'm comfortable recommending this to Laura for exec signoff. If Marissa and Legal confirm the redline wording, we should prepare an approval memo (short bullet doc) and the DocuSign envelope.

1) Uplift cap: capped at 5% per year.
2) Renewal protection: limited to the immediate first renewal only; after that, market pricing applies.

Once Finance signs off on the margin, Legal should prepare the final DocuSign packet using the attached approval template and route to NovoMed procurement. Diego — please confirm expected signature timeline and that procurement will accept a DocuSign envelope with these redlines.

Approval granted conditional on the above controls. Thank you for the concise pack.
